title: Rotate a List to the Right
statement:
Rotate the linked list to the **right** by `k` places: every node moves `k` positions towards the end, and the nodes that fall off the end come back at the front (in the same order). Return the head of the rotated list.

`k` can be much larger than the length of the list.

examples.explanation: The last two nodes (4 and 5) move to the front.
Rotating by 4 is the same as rotating by 4 mod 3 = 1.

hints.nudge: Rotating by the length of the list brings you back to the start. So how many rotations do you really have to do?
hints.pattern: Count the length, reduce k modulo the length, make the list circular, and cut it at the right place.
hints.pseudocode:
if list is empty or has one node: return head
length = number of nodes; tail = last node
k = k mod length; if k == 0: return head
tail.next = head          (make a ring)
newTail = the node at position length - k - 1 (counting from 0)
newHead = newTail.next; newTail.next = null
return newHead
hints.walkthrough: Rotating one place at a time would be O(n * k) and k can be a billion. First find the length n and the last node in one pass. Rotating by n changes nothing, so use k mod n; if that is 0 there is nothing to do. Now join the last node to the first to form a ring. In the rotated list the old node at position n - k becomes the head, so the node before it, at position n - k - 1 (counting from 0), becomes the new last node: walk to it, take its next as the new head, and set its next to null to break the ring. O(n) time, O(1) memory.
